summary: Iteration 14 (Fase A — Mesas + Sala) fully verified. Backend: 11/11 new table tests + 34/35 regression (1 pre-existing flaky WS test on cash-register-close, unrelated to Tables). Frontend: /tables renders with stats, CRUD (create/edit/delete), reserve→unreserve, open→POS(pos-active-table-banner + waiter)→checkout→auto-close→/tables navigation, walk-in (/pos?walk=1 no banner). All required data-testids present.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py — PUT /api/tables/{id}/bill does NOT clear opened_at/waiter fields (only sets status). This is fine per Fase A (bill is a transient status), but consider whether current_order_id should also be set when going through this endpoint. Not blocking.

server.py — PUT /api/tables/{id}/open uses `{$set: opened_at: datetime.utcnow()}` — Motor persists as naïve datetime. Consistent with other timestamps in the codebase but consider timezone.utc for future-proofing.

server.py — In create_order, when order.table_id is provided but the table does not belong to the current tenant, the update silently no-ops (matched_count=0 not checked). Not a security issue (write scoped by restaurant_id) but the client will believe the table was billed. Consider raising 400 when matched_count=0.
TablesPage.jsx — handleClose uses window.confirm which is not testable in Playwright without dialog handler; consider a shadcn AlertDialog for consistency with the rest of the app.

POSPage.jsx — pos-active-table-banner text does not always include 'Mesero: X'. When a mesa is opened without a waiter and without an active cashier (edge case reproduced during this test session), the banner shows 'Mesa N · X personas' only. The spec text 'Mesero: Y' becomes optional; UI handles this gracefully with `${activeTable.waiter_name ? …}`. Not a bug.

TablesPage.jsx — All CRUD paths call `load()` after the mutation AND rely on WS 'table.*' events to also call `load()`. This double-fires load() on the actor's own client; harmless but slightly wasteful.

success_rate.backend: 100% new (11/11 tables) + 97% regression (34/35, 1 pre-existing flaky cash-register-close WS test — same as iter 13)
